subject.title: [Feature]: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level

question: Should OpenClaw add native core/gateway per-agent spend-budget enforcement, and what minimal contract should the first version own across limits, reset windows, reservations, receipts, and operator UX?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses config shape, provider admission policy, durable accounting, fail-open/fail-closed semantics, cron/unattended workflows, and status/doctor UX, so automation cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Design a native gateway budget contract
options.body: Implement a minimal opt-in per-agent budget surface with durable pre-dispatch reservations, post-run receipts, visible status, and doctor/setup recovery before expanding policy modes.

options.title: Expose only plugin hooks
options.body: Keep core lean by improving plugin APIs for pre-run blocking and leave budget policy to plugins or ClawHub integrations.

options.title: Defer to provider limits
options.body: Close or defer native enforcement and document provider-side quotas as the supported spend-control path for now.

recommendation.title: Design a native gateway budget contract
recommendation.body: Implement a minimal opt-in per-agent budget surface with durable pre-dispatch reservations, post-run receipts, visible status, and doctor/setup recovery before expanding policy modes.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is recent work across the gateway/config/agent runtime paths that would own the native contract.
